To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the physician's role as coordinator of the weight reduction program is essential.

the most important factors in weight loss are: 1) a reduction in energy intake, 2) an increase in physical activity, 3) a reduction in fat intake, 4) a reduction in the intake of alcohol, 5) the use of a low-calorie, low-fat diet, 6) a reduction in carbohydrate intake, 7) a reduction in protein intake, and 8) the use of exercise.
the most important factor in successful weight reduction therapy is motivation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of an educational and motivational program for obese patients.
the development of a model of the doctor-patient interaction in the management of obese patients.
understanding the nature and causes of overweight, and the development of a rational and effective approach to weight control.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the physician has an important role in the management of overweight and obesity.
the doctor and the patient should work as a team in the management of the obese patient.
the doctor's and the patient's roles and responsibilities should be clearly defined and that the doctor should be the coordinator of a weight reduction therapy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to demonstrate that the physician can play a major role in the treatment of obesity.
the patient's and the physician's problems in treating obesity are not the same.
we have shown that a physician can help patients lose weight and keep the weight off.
The main takeaway from our work is that
physicians should not only be aware of their role in the weight loss process, but also of the fact that their role is not to be the only person in the weight loss journey of the patient.
we should be more careful in our use of the terms 'overweight' and 'obesity'.
physicians should be more aware of their role in weight management and should be more proactive.
